title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: §39 of E526 treats Case V, transverse vibrations of an elastic rod (Euler–Bernoulli beam) with end E (s=0) simply supported (pinned) and end F (s=a) clamped. The mode shape is y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k))·(α e^{uω} + β e^{-uω} + γ sin uω + δ cos uω), with u = s/a and ω = a/f. The pinned end gives β = −α and δ = 0. The clamped end (y = 0, y' = 0) gives α(e^ω − e^{-ω}) + γ sin ω = 0 and α(e^ω + e^{-ω}) + γ cos ω = 0.

On this page Euler eliminates α/γ from the two conditions. This gives the frequency equation tan ω = (e^ω − e^{-ω})/(e^ω + e^{-ω}), i.e. tan ω = tanh ω. He notes that this is identical to the equation of his Case II.

Writing S = e^ω − e^{-ω} and K = e^ω + e^{-ω}, one has S² + K² = 2(e^{2ω} + e^{-2ω}). So sin ω = ±S/√(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})) and cos ω = ±K/√(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})), with sin and cos of the same sign. Hence α/γ = ∓1/√(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})). Normalising α = 1 gives β = −1, δ = 0 and γ = ∓√(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})). The upper sign applies when sin ω and cos ω are both positive, the lower when both are negative.

The mode shape is therefore y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k))·(e^{uω} − e^{-uω} ∓ √(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})) sin uω). In modern form this is φ(x) ∝ sinh βx − (sinh βL / sin βL) sin βx, the standard clamped–pinned mode.

The frequency relation √(2g/k) = ω²c√(2gb)/a² is carried over from earlier cases. It gives a period of πa²/(ω²c√(2gb)) and a sound (frequency) of ω²c√(2gb)/(πa²), i.e. frequency ∝ ω²/L².

Corollary 1 (§40) begins: since the equation coincides with Case II, its roots are the same. On the next page these are given as ω ≈ 5π/4, 9π/4, …; the true roots are 3.9266, 7.0686, …, slightly below (4n+1)π/4.
errors: No substantive error on this page. The algebra (S² + K² = 2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω}), the same-sign condition for sin and cos, and the ratio α/γ) checks out.

The roots of tan ω = tanh ω are only approximately (4n+1)π/4; the first is 3.92660 versus 5π/4 = 3.92699. Euler presents them as the values (on the next page, citing Case II), so they should be read as approximations. The relative error is about 1e-4 for the first root and decreases exponentially.
Minor notational ambiguity in the print: '√2g/k' should read √(2g/k), consistent with the time factor sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)).

ideas.what: Frequency equation tan ω = tanh ω for a clamped–pinned elastic beam, with roots ≈ (4n+1)π/4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1740s), fully systematised by Euler in E526 (1779/1782); later standard in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; related beam vibration results in Euler's 1744 Methodus inveniendi (Additamentum I) and the Bernoulli–Euler correspondence; discussed in Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Explicit mode shape sinh − (sinh ω/sin ω)·sin, written as e^{uω} − e^{-uω} ∓ √(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})) sin uω
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526); standard in later engineering texts

ideas.what: Observation that the clamped–pinned case shares its frequency equation with another boundary case (Case II, presumably free–pinned), yet has different mode shapes
ideas.modern_name: Coincidence of the nonzero spectra of clamped–pinned and free–pinned beams (a known duality between boundary conditions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Known in the classical literature (Rayleigh; Truesdell's commentary on Euler)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct derivation of the clamped–pinned beam frequency equation and mode shape in a well-known, well-studied paper (E526, covered by Truesdell). The coincidence with Case II is also stated by Euler himself and is classically known. Nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In the frequency relation, the left side should be √(2g/k), not √(2g)/k.
The image shows 'sin.u ω' and 'e^{uω}' correctly; the transcription is otherwise faithful.
